summary: The central cone-universality proof constructs zero cross weights for nonzero zero-diagonal block targets; its dimension and error-budget expressions also do not support the stated quantitative theorem. A different explicit cone construction restores qualitative universality with a changed bound. No impossibility of universality or benchmark failure is claimed.
limitations: No author code executed; no benchmark reproduction.
The demonstrated counterexample refutes the printed block construction, not qualitative universality.
Printed quantitative bound not restored; alternative bound and proof supplied.
Most empirical appendices, prior training, raw runs and external references not audited.

problems.claim: AppendixA.4's cone feature assignment exactly realizes every nonnegative block matrix, yielding Theorem3.8.
problems.check: Printed same-sign s=-t gives all Lorentz products0,not unit cross weight; K4 diagnostic gives identical cancellation. Original dimensions negative/noninteger and error budget also invalid.
problems.result: Core constructive derivation invalid; qualitative theorem not disproved.
problems.counterevidence: p4 opposite-sign bipartite construction is valid; a general corrected block representation and independent qualitative proof are supplied.
problems.impact: Central probability-universality proof and printed quantitative guarantee require correction; empirical outcomes not refuted.
problems.correction: Use one diagonal coordinate and one opposite-sign coordinate per unordered block pair; epsilon/3 slack; explicit changed dimension bound. General repair verified,author adoption unknown.

independent_verification.source_and_assumptions: Read p5 Definition3.3, p6 Definition3.4/Theorem3.8, pp15-16 A.4; directly viewed p16 signs. Symmetric nonnegative block target with zero diagonal/unit off-diagonals and cone |s|<=t is admissible.
independent_verification.decisive_reasoning: The printed coordinates put s=-t at both ends of every nonzero cross channel. Hence t_i dot t_j - s_i dot s_j=0 for every pair of zero-diagonal target classes, irrespective of class-count size. For K2 the two channels also collide at3, but correcting indexing alone leaves cancellation. Literal dimension signs and epsilon+epsilon/2 budget fail independently; charitable squaring of -log does not fix construction or budget.
independent_verification.alternative_and_dependency: The cone itself permits opposite exclusive signs, as the paper already illustrates in the bipartite case. Thus the finding refutes the central printed constructive proof, not qualitative universality or experiments.
independent_verification.severity_and_repair: Major retained because exact block representation is the necessary link in probability-valued universality Theorem3.8. Independently verified repair: diagonal coordinates contribute only b_ii; each unordered pair coordinate with t=a on both ends, s=+a/-a and a=sqrt(b_ij/2) contributes exactly b_ij between classes and0 within. All coordinates satisfy the cone. The report energy-refinement proof increases normalized L2 energy by >eta^2, at most R^2 total, with <=4-fold partition growth. Setting delta=eta=epsilon/3 gives D_square<=2epsilon/3<epsilon and the changed dimension bound; this does not validate the original bound.

title: PieClam: A Universal Graph Autoencoder Based on Overlapping Inclusive and Exclusive Communities
acceptance_scope: Focused independent acceptance of the block-construction finding, including its dimension/tolerance subfindings and the entire proposed qualitative repair. Main comparison experiments and unrelated code paths remain outside this acceptance.
